runtime.execution: Jupyter messages over ZMQ with separate control thread; Python/IPython shell, asyncio execution and optional threaded subshells.
runtime.service_boundary: Kernel is an independent computation service; a harness should consume its protocol rather than infer ownership from locality.

summary: Persistent code execution, rich replies, history queries and separate control channel; restart continuity is not live-object persistence.

inspection.scope: Read namespace initialization, execute/result handling, SIGINT and shutdown, history dispatch, subshell manager and selected tests.
inspection.limits: IPython/Jupyter client dependencies are not independently audited; arbitrary native/foreign code cancellation and serialization not established.

actions.lifecycle: Persistent shell; async or blocking execution.
actions.authority: Authorized kernel client; host-process code authority

actions.output: Thread-backed execution route or unknown-subshell error

evidence.claim: User namespace is assigned to a persistent IPython shell.
Code is transformed and dispatched to blocking or asynchronous IPython cell runner with optional history.
Reply includes error traceback/type/value, execution counter, user expressions and partial payloads.
Interrupt sends SIGINT to process or process group on POSIX; Windows message interrupt unsupported here.
Shutdown reply carries restart flag, then stops control and shell loops; not namespace snapshot.
Tail/range/search dispatch to history manager, with raw/output flags.
Manager owns subshell thread/socket lifetime and serializes cache mutations/sends; control thread routes separately.
SIGINT cancels async future in main thread; subshells cannot use that signal handler.

tests.focus: Unicode history export and signal/message interruption of input().
tests.oracle: History file must contain exact source including abcþ; interrupt test validates execute_reply parent ID, not completeness of stdout or foreign-call termination.

tests.focus: Overlapping subshell execution with shared variables.
tests.oracle: Barrier/sleep assertions establish expected overlap and execute_reply status; time-sensitive test is skipped under coverage.

strengths: An explicit computation consumer/service boundary and structured execution identity.
Separate control traffic and history retrieval are useful even without agent machinery.
limits: Kernel history is narrower than a complete original audit.
Interrupt acknowledgement and restart flags cannot be treated as universal cancellation or memory continuity.
arconaut_questions: How does a harness pause only its requests and standing programs while other clients continue using a shared kernel?
What values/handles must be serialized or reacquired independently of the kernel process?
